en-GB.name: Glint: Sun Mirror
en-GB.subtitle: Catch the sun, pop the shadows
en-GB.description:
The top half of your iPhone Duo is a mirror.

Open the phone and the mirror catches the sunrise, throwing a band of warm light across the garden below. The wider you open it, the further the light reaches. Close it a little and the light comes back towards the crease. Shut the phone and it's dark.

Shadows seep out of the crease and creep towards your five flowers. Hold the light on one and it sizzles, shrinks and pops in a burst of gold sparks and petals. Sweep through a crowd and the pops climb a rising scale. Sweep!

Spare the fireflies. They drift out of the crease too, and a firefly that reaches your flowers replants a lost one.

No ads. No in-app purchases. No accounts. No data collected. Pay once and it's yours.

THE LIGHT IS YOUR AIM
• The phone's angle is where the light lands, smoothly, both ways. Open wider to chase a shadow outwards, close a little to catch the next one at the crease
• Shadows never stand still, so a light left in one place only gives each a short dose. Follow the big ones as they creep
• Quick pops build a chain, up to ×4. Three or more in one sweep is a Sweep, with a bonus
• Light held on a firefly too long makes it fizzle and breaks your chain. A quick pass over one is safe
• A shadow that reaches the edge eats a flower. Lose all five and the night wins

FIVE KINDS OF SHADOW
Murks creep. Wisps come in quick little flocks. Brutes are big, slow and grumpy, and have to be followed. Splitters pop into two wisps flung further out. Hoppers crouch and jump, and the first touch of light makes them hop at once.

30 SUNRISES, 3 WORLDS
Every level is one sunrise, about a minute long, with the sun climbing in the mirror as the clock runs. At sunrise every shadow left melts away. Keep all five flowers for three stars. Stars open the next world: the Meadow, the Rooftops and the Harbour, where it gets properly hard.

LONG NIGHT
Endless waves that never let up, and one best score to beat.

TODAY'S DAWN
One sunrise a day, the same for everyone. Your best of the day counts.

NO TUTORIAL TO SIT THROUGH
Level 1 teaches as you play, one line at a time: close the phone to start, open it to let the light in, light the shadows.

MADE FOR THE FOLD. PLAYS ON OTHER iPhone MODELS TOO.
On iPhone Duo, hold it however you like, as a laptop or as a book: one half is the mirror, the other is the garden. Play lives between about a right angle and well open, so you never lay the phone flat or rush the hinge. Every sunrise starts with the phone shut, and shutting it mid-level pauses the game. Settings can swap the halves. On any other iPhone, drag anywhere to aim the light, and a brass lever on the mirror follows your finger.

SOUND AND FEEL
A sizzle that swells with everything in the light, a bright pluck for every pop that climbs the scale as your chain grows, a chord for every Sweep, birdsong at sunrise. All synthesised live in the app. You feel the sizzle in your hands and a crisp tick for every pop. Sound, music, haptics and Reduce motion each have a setting.

GAME CENTER
Leaderboards for the Long Night, Today's Dawn and your total stars, and 10 achievements. Optional: Glint works fully without signing in.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No accounts, no tracking, no data collected. Your progress stays on your iPhone.

review.notes:
NO LOGIN - this game has no accounts. There is nothing to sign in to and no demo account to give: open the app and tap Play.

Thanks for reviewing Glint: Sun Mirror, a paid game with no ads, no in-app purchases, no data collection and no network requests of its own.

1. TESTING ON A REGULAR iPHONE (start here)
You don't need an iPhone Duo. The whole game plays on any iPhone (iOS 18 or later) and in the Simulator. Portrait is best.
- The top of the screen is a brass-framed mirror; the bottom is the garden. The line between them is the crease.
- Control: drag anywhere, up or down, like a trackpad. A band of gold light moves across the garden and a brass lever on the mirror follows. Drag down to send the light further from the crease, up to bring it back.
- Quickest look (about a minute): Home > Play starts Level 1. The hint says "Drag down to let the light in". Shadows (inky blobs with eyes) creep out of the crease towards five flowers at the far edge. Keep the light on a shadow and it sizzles and pops. At sunrise (about 60 s) the level ends with 1 to 3 stars.
- Fireflies (small glowing dots) drift out too: light held on one too long makes it fizzle; one that reaches the flowers replants a lost flower.
- A shadow that reaches the edge eats a flower. All five gone: "The night won" and Retry.

2. HOW THE HINGE IS USED (iPhone Duo)
Glint reads the hinge angle only through the public iOS 27.1 API (SwiftUI onHingeChange), behind an availability check. No private API. The angle is used only while playing; it is never stored or sent.
a) One half of the inner display is the mirror, the other the garden; the fold is the crease. Any pose works, like a laptop (mirror on top) or like a book. Settings > Swap halves flips the halves.
b) The opening angle is the aim. Shut is dark. As the phone opens, light pools in the crease; from about 80 degrees the band lifts out and moves across the garden, reaching the far edge at about 145 degrees. Opening further changes nothing, so the phone never needs to lie flat.
c) Every level starts with the phone shut: if it is open, the game says "Close the phone to start", then "Open the phone to let the light in".
d) Closing the phone (below about 15 degrees for a quarter of a second) pauses the level, and the outer display shows "Paused" with the score. Opening it again resumes after a short grace.
e) There is no pause, warning or penalty anywhere near 90 degrees.

3. KIND TO THE DEVICE (Guidelines 2.4.2 and 1.4.5)
- Play is small, smooth movements between about 80 and 145 degrees, inside the range where the hinge holds its position. Glint never asks the user to lay the phone flat, slam it or move it fast.
- The only full close is the one at the start of a level (and to pause), at the player's own pace.
- No score, achievement or leaderboard rewards hinge speed or the number of folds.

4. MODES AND PROGRESS (nothing hidden, nothing to buy)
- Levels: 30 sunrises in 3 worlds (Meadow, Rooftops, Harbour). Stars (by flowers kept) open the next levels and worlds.
- Today's Dawn: one seeded 90 s sunrise a day, the same for everyone; best of the day kept. Opens after level 3.
- Long Night: endless waves and one best score. Opens after level 5, or a day after the first launch.
- Level 1 is gentle and is won by anyone who moves the light at all.

5. CONTENT
Cartoon shadow critters made of ink, with big eyes. In the light they shrink and pop into gold sparks and petals. No blood, no injury, no death: an eaten flower becomes a drooping stalk and a firefly can replant it.

6. PRIVACY
No third-party SDKs, analytics, ads, accounts or tracking. Progress and settings stay on the device. App Privacy: Data Not Collected.

7. GAME CENTER
Optional, never required. 3 leaderboards (Long Night, Today's Dawn, Total Stars) and 10 achievements (435 points), none hidden.

8. OTHER
- No notifications. Debug and demo modes are disabled in Release builds.
- Sound plays with the silent switch on; Settings > Sound turns it off.

nomination.name: Glint: Sun Mirror - App Launch - iPhone Duo light game
nomination.description:
Glint turns the top half of iPhone Duo into a mirror. Open the phone and it catches the sunrise, throwing a band of light across the garden on the other half. The phone's angle is the aim: the wider you open it, the further the light reaches, smoothly and both ways, and shut means dark.

Shadow critters seep out of the crease towards five flowers. Light pops them in gold sparks and petals, and a sweep through a crowd climbs a rising scale of notes. Fireflies must be spared: they replant lost flowers. Five kinds of shadow each want a different move, from flocks of wisps to brutes that have to be followed.

30 handmade sunrises in three worlds, with stars to earn, then an endless Long Night and a daily Today's Dawn for everyone. Every level starts with the phone shut; shutting it pauses. Other iPhones aim the light by dragging. Every sound is synthesized in the app. No ads, no in-app purchases, no data collected.
nomination.notes: Optimized for iPhone Duo: one half is a mirror, the other the play field, in laptop or book pose. Public iOS 27.1 hinge API: the angle maps continuously to where the light lands, from 80 to 145 degrees, so play is gentle and never flat, with no pause near 90 degrees. Closing is a real pause; the outer display shows it. A new hinge verb for us: reach, aimed by angle. Also from us: Squish, Brim, Swoop, Hush and Snapjaw.
